effect_estimate.comment: OLS regression results (N = 500 systems; Table 2 prints note '*p , 0.05, **p , 0.0', an apparent typesetting truncation of p < 0.01) test private ownership, state PUC regulation of public utilities, and pro-private state regulatory regimes (NJ and PA: DSIC surcharges and fair market value statutes) on annual water bills and low-income water affordability.
effect_estimate.value: In multivariable OLS regressions across the 500 largest US community water systems (N = 500, 2015), private (investor) ownership vs. public ownership is associated with a $144.04 higher annual household water bill (Coeff. = 144.04**, Std. coeff. = 0.35**, adj. R2 = 0.32; unadjusted mean $501 vs. $315) and 1.55 percentage points more of lowest-quintile household income spent on water bills (Coeff. = 1.55**, Std. coeff. = 0.26**, adj. R2 = 0.45; unadjusted mean 4.39% vs. 2.84%). State regulation favorable to private operators (New Jersey and Pennsylvania) is associated with an $88.64 higher annual water bill (Coeff. = 88.64**, Std. coeff. = 0.17**) and a non-significant +0.46 percentage point difference in lowest-quintile income share (Coeff. = 0.46, Std. coeff. = 0.06). State PUC regulation of public water utilities shows no statistically significant association with annual water bills (Coeff. = 36.43, Std. coeff. = 0.06) or lowest-quintile income share (Coeff. = 0.29, Std. coeff. = 0.03).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 6, Methods; PDF p. 8, Results; PDF p. 9, Table 2; PDF p. 10, Discussion

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines household water tariffs, recurring drinking water-related fees, and regulatory capital-recovery surcharges (such as Distribution System Improvement Charges [DSIC] and fair-market-value rate recovery) across public vs. private utilities and state PUC regulatory regimes.

study_design.comment: Compiles January 2015 rate schedules for the 500 largest US community water systems, links them with 2011-2015 ACS socioeconomic data and 2015 US Drought Monitor data, and estimates multivariable OLS regression models.
study_design.value: Cross-sectional observational study of community water systems using multivariable ordinary least squares (OLS) regression
